title: Daemon access and API compatibility
summary: A declared local socket must reach a Linux Engine with a compatible API. Socket absence, access denial and an unsupported API are different boundaries. Docker contexts and rootless sockets can point to different daemons.
checks: Confirm the approved socket and daemon identity from the affected user and namespace.
Check service state and socket permissions independently; repeat the fixed version request.
limitations: A successful version request does not verify any container or workload.
